_meta.rendered_by: src/styles/build-tokens.ts into src/styles/tokens.css (committed, byte-compared by tokens.test.ts)
_meta.surfaces: "every-surface" in an on-list stands for every role: surface token that has no notEverySurface, derived when the check runs (contrast.ts), so a surface added later is checked against every ink without an edit here. paper opts out on the token. fill, a control's wash, is a surface (Q1 (A)), so every-surface includes it; the inks that sit on a control still name it beside every-surface, so the pair is visible where it is read.

side.note: desktop sidebar; defined on the phone too, unused there

canvas.note: desktop canvas behind the paper; defined on the phone too, unused there

label2.note: secondary text, and placeholder text (WCAG 1.4.3 counts a placeholder as text)

label3.note: an icon glyph, a disabled glyph; never a color: for text and never in ::placeholder (roleUsageViolations). Alpha raised from the prototypes' 0.36/0.38 light and 0.32 dark so it clears 3:1 (Q1).

sep.exempt: WCAG 1.4.11: a separator is decorative; no component or state is perceived only through it

hover.exempt: WCAG 1.4.11: a hover wash is a transient affordance, never the only way to perceive a component or its state

selbg.exempt: WCAG 1.4.11: a selection wash is paired with aria-current and a tint-ink label; it is not the only signal

fill.note: a control's wash (a field, a segmented control's track), a surface like the other washes: every ink on every-surface is checked on it, composited over every opaque surface. Q1 (A), PO 2026-10-21 on PR #120: the wash is about 1.15:1 on white, so it is never a control's boundary; every selector that paints fill carries boundary too (fillBoundaryViolations, run on the built CSS).

boundary.note: the visible edge of a field or a segmented control's track, in a border, an outline or an inset box-shadow ring; every selector that paints fill carries it (fillBoundaryViolations). Q1 (A), PO 2026-10-21 on PR #120: non-text at 3:1 on bg, bg2 and bg3, derived from label3 so it follows it.

recv.note: a received bubble and the paper card in the chat, whose top band can be the NOW fill. One dark value for both layouts: the desktop prototype's #2c2c2f put the NOW band at 2.94:1 (Q1).

sent.note: the sent bubble and the send button: both prototypes paint them on bg (the thread, and the composer's field)

focus.note: the focus ring (:focus-visible outline, a focused field's border): the phone prototype's full-tint ring in both layouts. The desktop prototype's color-mix(tint 60%, transparent) is 2.5:1 on white, under WCAG 1.4.11's 3:1 (Q1). Derived from tint so it follows it.

mio-bg.notEverySurface: only Mio's head image is painted on it (the chat avatar, the voice orb, the sidebar mark): no text, no wash, no fill

now.note: Part B decision 7: the one NOW red. Checked at 3:1 against every surface the prototypes put a NOW fill on: the page and its cards (bg, bg2, bg3), the sidebar's status dot (side), the desktop canvas, the paper card in the chat (recv) and the bars; never on a THIS_WEEK, tint or unknown wash. No desktop override: light is #d12c24 in both layouts. Every other now-* token derives from it.

green.note: the follow-up circle carries meaning, so WCAG 1.4.11's 3:1 applies. Light changed from the prototypes' #34c759 (2.2:1 on white) (Q1).

paper.notEverySurface: only paper-ink is painted on it: the paper is the photo's frame, not an app surface
paper.note: the paper stays light in the dark theme, as paper does

bar.note: translucent: the navigation and tab bars

scrim.exempt: WCAG 1.4.11: a modal scrim dims what is behind a sheet; the sheet, not the scrim, is the component
